The operation ${R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1}$ means that we need to multiply the first row of the matrix by $\frac{1}{3}.$

Multiplying the first row by $\frac{1}{3}$, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\begin{bmatrix}6 & -6 & 0 \\ 6 & 0 & 6 \\ -6 & 6 & 6\end{bmatrix}\quad {R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\ & \sim \begin{bmatrix}\frac{1}{3}\cdot (6) & \frac{1}{3}\cdot (-6) & \frac{1}{3}\cdot (0) \\ 6 & 0 & 6 \\ -6 & 6 & 6\end{bmatrix} \\ & \sim \begin{bmatrix}2 & -2 & 0 \\ 6 & 0 & 6 \\ -6 & 6 & 6\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

The operation ${R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2}$ means that we need to multiply the second row of the matrix by $\frac{1}{3}.$

Multiplying the second row by $\frac{1}{3}$, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\begin{bmatrix}6 & -6 & 0 \\ 6 & 0 & 6 \\ -6 & 6 & 6\end{bmatrix}\quad {R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\ & \sim \begin{bmatrix}6 & -6 & 0 \\ \frac{1}{3}\cdot (6) & \frac{1}{3}\cdot (0) & \frac{1}{3}\cdot (6) \\ -6 & 6 & 6\end{bmatrix} \\ & \sim \begin{bmatrix}6 & -6 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 2 \\ -6 & 6 & 6\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$
